title: Production Decision Intelligence: From Fragmented Operational Data to Action
shortDescription: Sanitized case study on Python/SQL pipelines, quality controls, forecasting, exception analytics, and governed decision workflows across 1,679 operational projects.
situation: Operational data was fragmented across project, scheduling, and financial systems, delaying exception detection and increasing reconciliation effort.
task: Design production decision-intelligence workflows that turn multi-system data into timely, governed operational actions.
actionNonTech: Mapped decision points where forecasts, anomaly signals, and exception queues should trigger review or automation. Prioritized reconciliation and monitoring use cases with measurable operational actions.
actionTech: Built Python/SQL pipelines with quality controls, forecasting and exception analytics, operational monitoring (414 targeted alerts, 171 automated workflows), and governed LLM/agent workflows (1,243 agent runs; 4,522 logged actions) across 1,679 projects representing ~$22M estimated revenue.
resultBusiness: 50%+ reconciliation-effort reduction; key signal latency under 5 minutes; approximately $25K/month PROJECTED SAVINGS (projected, not realized).
resultTech: Production pipelines with multi-system integrations, anomaly/exception analytics, and governed agent logging for inspectable decision workflows.

title: Customer / Credit Card Offer Optimization
shortDescription: Academic project on personalizing credit-card offers with classification, segmentation, and evaluation metrics — not a production bank deployment.
situation: Academic case context: a financial institution wants better targeting for credit-card offers while balancing approval efficiency and compliance constraints.
task: Build and evaluate predictive models and customer segments for offer targeting as an analytical learning project.
actionNonTech: Framed targeting as a decision problem: who to contact, under what constraints, and how to evaluate lift without claiming production adoption.
actionTech: Built logistic regression and gradient boosting models in Python (scikit-learn, XGBoost). Applied K-Means segmentation and reporting automation for iterative evaluation.
resultBusiness: Academic Project: model and segment evaluation suggested improved targeting efficiency in held-out analysis. Results are analytical findings only — not realized bank revenue, campaign lift, or production adoption.
resultTech: Reported ROC-AUC and automation of recurring evaluation reports for faster iteration in the academic setting.

title: City of Rochester Resource-Allocation Decision Support
shortDescription: Classification, A/B testing, uplift modeling, and survey analytics supporting City of Rochester resource-allocation decisions.
situation: City stakeholders needed evidence-based prioritization from survey and program data to allocate limited resources.
task: Deliver classification, experimentation, and reporting that connect survey signals to decision support.
actionNonTech: Aligned model outputs and experiments with stakeholder decision questions around resource allocation and intervention targeting.
actionTech: Built classification and uplift models on 5,000+ survey responses; applied TF-IDF, topic modeling, and clustering; delivered Power BI / SQL reporting.
resultBusiness: Improved classifier discrimination by +0.07 AUC and reduced reporting effort by approximately 50%, supporting clearer resource-allocation discussions.
resultTech: End-to-end analytics stack: SQL, uplift/classification modeling, text analytics, and Power BI decision dashboards.

title: Production Quality & Process Optimization
shortDescription: Consulting analysis of production-line variability and fill-weight stability using statistical process control and temporal diagnostics.
situation: A manufacturing client needed clearer visibility into production-line variability and fill-weight stability across package types and work centers.
task: Apply statistical process-control and temporal diagnostics to characterize sources of variability and support process-control discussions.
actionNonTech: Scoped the analytical questions with operations stakeholders and translated diagnostic findings into discussion-ready process-control priorities.
actionTech: Applied statistical process control, temporal diagnostics, and Python-based visual analysis to production and checkweight-style measurements.
resultBusiness: Analytical findings identified meaningful sources of production variability and supported process-control discussions. No realized financial or yield impact is claimed.
resultTech: Reproducible diagnostic workflow combining SPC-style charts and temporal summaries for manufacturing review.

title: Governed LLM & Agent Workflows for Operational Decisions
shortDescription: Governed agent workflows with validation gates, human approval, and logged actions supporting production decision analytics.
situation: Operators needed natural-language and workflow assistance without losing auditability of actions taken on operational data.
task: Introduce governed LLM/agent workflows that log actions and remain subordinate to the decision-systems foundation.
actionNonTech: Defined where agent assistance is appropriate versus where deterministic rules and human review remain required.
actionTech: Implemented governed agent workflows with validation gates, human approval, and action logging — 1,243 agent runs and 4,522 logged actions — integrated with operational monitoring and exception queues.
resultBusiness: 1,243 agent runs and 4,522 logged actions created an auditable action history for AI-assisted operational workflows.
resultTech: Action-logged agent workflows connected to production monitoring and reconciliation contexts, with human approval retained in the governance path.

title: NAVAN IPO Analysis
shortDescription: Independent analysis of NAVAN's IPO in a constrained market window using public financial and IPO market data.
situation: In October 2025, Navan went public during constrained U.S. IPO activity, raising questions about investor appetite versus valuation compression.
task: Assess whether the listing signaled renewed optimism or continued discipline in growth-technology valuations.
actionNonTech: Applied structured market-context framing comparing liquidity, risk appetite, and IPO activity against prior periods.
actionTech: Compiled public financial and IPO market data; modeled revenue and valuation scenarios in Python/Excel; produced a visualization deck.
resultBusiness: Analytical Finding: the listing is consistent with disciplined market reopening rather than speculative optimism. Independent analysis only — not client advisory outcomes.
resultTech: Data-verified presentation integrating IPO statistics and multi-scenario valuation framing.
